residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must have been ordinarily resident in Manitoba for at least one year immediately before the divorce application (Divorce Act, RSC 1985, c. 3, s.3(1)).

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing. The one-year separation must be complete before or at the time the divorce order is granted.

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: Spouses have lived separate and apart for at least one year immediately preceding the determination of the divorce application.

fault.name: Physical or Mental Cruelty
fault.description: The respondent has treated the applicant with physical or mental cruelty of such a kind as to render intolerable the continued cohabitation of the spouses.

terminology.alimony: Maintenance (Manitoba terminology under the Family Maintenance Act, CCSM c. F20 — not 'spousal support')
terminology.maritalProperty: Family Property (Family Property Act, CCSM c. F25)

legalCitations.description: Federal divorce statute — governs divorce proceedings in all provinces and territories

legalCitations.code: Family Property Act, CCSM c. F25
legalCitations.description: Manitoba statute — equalization of family property on marriage breakdown

legalCitations.code: Family Maintenance Act, CCSM c. F20
legalCitations.description: Manitoba statute — maintenance and child support obligations

legalCitations.description: Federal guidelines for calculating child support amounts

basic.name: Petition for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding in the Court of King's Bench of Manitoba

basic.name: Divorce Order
basic.description: Draft order to be submitted to court for signature

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Federal Child Support Guidelines apply in all provinces. Manitoba enforces through the Maintenance Enforcement Program (MEP).

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: SSAG are advisory only — not legislatively mandated but widely applied by Manitoba courts. Manitoba uses the term 'maintenance' (Family Maintenance Act, CCSM c. F20) rather than 'spousal support' in provincial proceedings.

effectiveDateRule: 31 days after the divorce order is made, unless the court varies the effective date or both parties waive the waiting period (Divorce Act, s.12).
certificateNote: A Certificate of Divorce may be obtained from the court office after the effective date of the Divorce Order (Divorce Act, s.12(7)).

filingFees.notes: Manitoba filing fee for a Petition for Divorce is approximately CAD $200. Fee waiver may be available for low-income parties.
